science.assessment: Closed-gas piston boundary work is distinguished from net force on the piston. Quasistatic motion, negligible piston friction/inertia, and approximately uniform gas pressure qualify use of gas pressure as total external pressure. A short displacement alone is not claimed to ensure constant pressure; negligible pressure variation within the interval is explicitly required. The force-area-volume derivation preserves the original formulas and labels.

Signed volume change is retained. Gas work is positive for expansion and negative for compression; work on the gas has the opposite sign. Cancellation of work is restricted to the same moving contact boundary and displacement, not generalized from Newton's third law to arbitrary bodies. Work transfers energy but is not equated to the total internal-energy or temperature change when heat exchange may also occur.

Extension to other systems is restricted to pressure-volume boundary work under the stated pressure and quasistatic conditions, not all work or arbitrary irreversible processes. Finite isobaric work is distinguished from local constant-pressure approximation and variable-pressure summation. The ideal-gas isothermal example specifies fixed quantity/composition. Graph vertical lengths correctly represent pressure; area gives the magnitude and process direction supplies the work sign. The original area-proof prompt is retained.
